record.prompt: how does a decision tree works?

relationship.statement: A decision tree classifies samples by recursively splitting data along feature thresholds that maximize impurity reduction. Each branch routes points to child nodes until regions are pure enough to predict a majority class.
assumptions: Binary classification (Class A vs. Class B) using axis-aligned threshold splits.
Node impurity is measured by Gini impurity, G = 1 - p_A^2 - p_B^2.
Dataset size is fixed at N = 20 samples across two features.

quantities.label: Root split x
quantities.meaning: Threshold on feature x used at the root node to send samples left or right.

quantities.label: Child split y
quantities.meaning: Second-level threshold on feature y applied to refine a mixed child node.

quantities.label: Class separation
quantities.meaning: Distance between the two class clusters in feature space.

quantities.label: Total samples N
quantities.meaning: Total number of labeled training samples evaluated at the root node.

quantities.label: Parent Gini G_0
quantities.meaning: Gini impurity of the unsplit root node before applying any threshold.

quantities.label: Weighted child Gini
quantities.meaning: Size-weighted average Gini impurity of the left and right root branches.

quantities.label: Impurity reduction
quantities.meaning: Drop in Gini impurity achieved by the root split (G_0 minus weighted child Gini).

quantities.label: Left branch count
quantities.meaning: Number of samples satisfying x <= split_x routed to the left branch.

quantities.label: Right branch count
quantities.meaning: Number of samples satisfying x > split_x routed to the right branch.

quantities.label: Tree accuracy
quantities.meaning: Percentage of samples correctly classified by majority vote at the leaves.
